ui_elements.label: Introduction paragraph
ui_elements.text: Void is a general purpose operating system, based on the monolithic Linux kernel. Its package system allows you to quickly install, update and remove software; software is provided in binary packages or can be built directly from sources with the help of the XBPS source packages collection.

ui_elements.label: Introduction paragraph
ui_elements.text: It is available for a variety of platforms. Software packages can be built natively or cross compiled through the XBPS source packages collection.

ui_elements.label: Introduction paragraph
ui_elements.text: Follow us on Mastodon, visit the #voidlinux IRC channel on libera.chat, and join the Void Linux subreddit.

ui_elements.label: Introduction paragraph
ui_elements.text: Visit the Void build server console for package build status updates.

ui_elements.label: Introduction paragraph
ui_elements.text: Contribute to the Void Linux project by adding and updating packages and extending the documentation. More information can be found in the Handbook.

ui_elements.label: Void Linux is an independent distribution, developed entirely by volunteers.
ui_elements.text: Void Linux is an independent distribution, developed entirely by volunteers.

ui_elements.label: Unlike trillions of other existing distros, Void is not a modification of an existing distribution. Void's package manager and build system have been written from scratch.
ui_elements.text: Unlike trillions of other existing distros, Void is not a modification of an existing distribution. Void's package manager and build system have been written from scratch.

ui_elements.label: Void focuses on stability, rather than on being bleeding-edge. Install once, update routinely and safely.
ui_elements.text: Void focuses on stability, rather than on being bleeding-edge. Install once, update routinely and safely.

ui_elements.label: Thanks to our continuous build system, new software is built into binary packages as soon as the changes are pushed to the void-packages repository.
ui_elements.text: Thanks to our continuous build system, new software is built into binary packages as soon as the changes are pushed to the void-packages repository.

ui_elements.label: We use runit as the init system and service supervisor.
ui_elements.text: We use runit as the init system and service supervisor.

ui_elements.label: runit is a simple and effective approach to initialize the system with reliable service supervision. Refer to the Void Handbook for an introduction.
